# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Need | Pick | Price (from the sources) |
|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (list $299) |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $125-$180 |
| Best for long runs and rain | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 |
| Best value | Nothing Ear (Open) | about $99 |
| Best budget hook style | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $79.99-$104 |
| Cheapest way to try the concept | JLab Flex Open / SoundPeats PearlClip Pro | $40-$50 |

## Top picks

- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** have the best sound of the clip-ons and physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. They last 7 hours per charge (19.5-27 hours with the case, depending on the source) and are rated IPX4, so they're a weaker choice for heavy rain. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new open-ear model within about a month of that article, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** is the pick if awareness matters most. It's a bone-conduction neckband with extra air-conduction drivers for bass, a 12-hour battery, an IP55 rating, and physical buttons. The band can get in the way of a low ponytail or winter hats. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **Shokz OpenDots 2** is WIRED's top open-earbud pick. It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating, and the reviewer wore it in the rain and submerged it without problems. It costs $200. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Nothing Ear (Open)** is SoundGuys' best open-ear pick and its best for running. It has strong bass for this category, a parametric EQ, and an IP54 rating. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [SoundGuys workout list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/))

## Budget options

- **Soundcore AeroFit 2** has an ear-hook design, a 10-hour battery, IP55 protection, and multipoint Bluetooth. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) is an affiliate link from the deal site Dealectric, which says code AFSC20 takes $25.99 off the $129.99 store price ($104). That's more than the $79.99 Amazon price SoundGuys lists, so compare before you buy. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2), [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **JLab Flex Open** is Runner's World's budget pick at about $40-$50 (the article gives both figures). It's comfortable and loud enough for most conditions, though it has less bass and detail. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **SoundPeats PearlClip Pro** is WIRED's cheap pick at $50. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))

## Things to know

- Open-ear sound is thinner than sealed earbuds, and it leaks at higher volumes. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
- The Bose and Shokz are close in quality. RTINGS says the Bose is slightly better for most people because it's more portable and doesn't press on your cheekbones or temples. The Shokz has the tougher IP55 rating and multi-device pairing. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946))
- I couldn't open direct product pages for most of these. The review articles linked above have current retailer buttons for Amazon, Best Buy, and the brands' own stores. Prices change, so check at checkout.

If you tell me your budget and whether you run in rain or wear glasses or hats, I can narrow this to one pick.
